lines: Matcha's founding engineer page says fully remote in the US, Canada, Europe, the UK, Brazil and Latin America.
But the founder's Hacker News post from October 12 says fully remote, anywhere in the world.
So can an engineer in India apply? One source says no. The other says yes.
So I built a small tool that reads a job's location text from one or more sources.
It returns allowed countries, time zones, EOR or contract setups, and visa sponsorship.
When the sources disagree, it says so, with a reason, instead of guessing.
Search Atlas is the same story. Its Hacker News post says anywhere. Its careers page lists six countries.
A clear post, like PrairieLearn's, comes back as US only, no visa sponsorship, no conflict.
I tested it on 32 real job posts with hand written labels. Half were held out while I wrote the rules.
On the held out half, the rules got every field right on 11 of 16 jobs, and the India answer right on all 16.
An LLM on Groq's free tier did worse, at 9 of 16. Every miss is listed in the repo.
The code, the cases, and the labels are public on GitHub.
